chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:
I asked him about a man who came to the Sacred Mosque, and he had intended the Hajj, can he circumambulate the House? He said: Yes, as long as he has not entered into Ihram.

key_terms.يُحْرِمْ: He enters into Ihram (state of consecration)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim perform Tawaf before entering Ihram if they have already intended Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of performing Tawaf al-Qudum (arrival circumambulation) prior to the formal declaration of Ihram, highlighting the flexibility in the sequence of Hajj rituals. It underscores the distinction between the internal intention (azm) and the external ritual state (ihram), a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of acts of worship performed before the specific time of Ihram entry.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,
‘I asked about a man who went to the Sacred Masjid, and he had been determined for the Hajj, can he circumambulate by the House (Kabah)?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, for as long as he has not worn Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who comes to Masjid al-Haram with the intention to commence al-Hajj, if he can perform Tawaf around the House. He (the Imam) said, ’Yes, as long as he has not assumed the state of Ihram.’”
